correctness.rationale: The actual pinned RESULT.md defines a free join of k>=2 compact full-dimensional factors A_i in pairwise independent affine blocks, with each d_i>=1, and uses the reflection definition (h+1)c-J subseteq hJ. Reflecting an arbitrary generating i-face forces (h+1)t_i-1>0 and the factor containment (h+1)t_i a_i-A_i subset ((h+1)t_i-1)A_i; hence that coefficient >=s(A_i). Summing yields h>=sum_i s(A_i)+k-1. Conversely choose t_i=(s(A_i)+1)/S, S=sum_i(s(A_i)+1): for a generator on face i, the reflected spatial block j has nonnegative join weight s(A_j)+1-delta_ij, and the i-block is in s(A_i)A_i by optimality of a_i. Convexity carries containment to all J. At equality each nonnegative lower-bound deficit vanishes separately, fixing barycentric weights and making every a_i an actual minimizing factor center. Injectivity at positive weights gives the full Cartesian-product center locus and affine dimension sum. This is a proof for all factors, not extrapolation from the LP examples; singleton factors and overlapping joins are outside the stated scope.

The formula has not been tested for degenerate point factors by the claimed positive-dimensional proof; no such extension is accepted.

value.rationale: Free join is a canonical convex-body composition operation. The result gives a new structural all-arity rule for a classical affine invariant independent of factor dimensions and a complete description of nonunique optimal-center sets, including additive dimensions. The invariant is natural before any numerical computation; the theorem controls smooth, nonsymmetric, and polyhedral inputs alike. Knowing asymmetry of factors does not by itself determine behavior of their join without the proved reflection containment.
residual_risks: This is a theorem about free joins, not arbitrary convex hulls; no downstream theorem or authorship/certification is asserted.

limitations: k>=2 and each affine factor dimension >=1; exact free joins only.
All-center locus is exact, not an independently measured empirical curve.
